RFC 8654 Section 3, rfc/full/rfc8654.txt:109-110: 'Peers that wish to use the BGP Extended Message Capability MUST support error handling for BGP UPDATE messages per [RFC7606].' This retains the prior composed receive-error-handling judgment, not a substitution of one ORIGIN case for all RFC 7606 obligations. Read the covering extended-message and forward-handle architecture documents, the unqualified summary row and derived ledger, the prior canonical composition, all eight distinct tagged test functions (fourteen tag carriers), the common classification/enforcement/synthesis producers, and the relevant RIB publication producers. No partial, gap or single-polarity annotation narrows this row. Obligation: RFC 7606 Section 2 requires actual removal of every contained route from Adj-RIB-In, not suppression of the malformed UPDATE; Section 7.1 says 'An UPDATE message with a malformed ORIGIN attribute SHALL be handled using the approach of treat-as-withdraw.' The changed test first installs both prefixes from an exactly 4097-octet UPDATE into real source storage and Loc-RIB and observes downstream announcements. It changes only ORIGIN to 3, then requires both routes absent from actual storage and Loc-RIB and both withdrawals on recipient TCP while retaining the source peer storage. Recovery reuses the same 4097-octet buffer, changing ORIGIN to 1 and MED to 17: both stored routes must contain those exact values, both prefixes must reach recipient TCP with each exact attribute, both actual Loc-RIB publications must carry Best.Metric 17, and both final selected paths must have Metric 17. Same Session identity, Established state and no source NOTIFICATION remain mandatory. Initial ORIGIN 0/MED 0 cannot satisfy the recovery assertions. Isolation/discrimination: the invalid frame is a clone differing only in ORIGIN; suppression of withdrawal, partial removal, session reset, lost recovery, stale attributes or stale selected metric fails a concrete assertion. The optional Forward handle is not an RFC obligation: rib_structured.go::handleReceivedStructured inserts routes before per-prefix election; rib_aigp.go::reselectAIGPRoutes elects stored routes with nil forward; rib_bestchange.go::checkRouteBestChange maps MED to Path.Metric; locrib/manager.go::insert does not dispatch an identical Path. This establishes a source-permitted nil-forward interleaving, not a runtime trace of that interleaving. The new oracle observes the selected-path contract without weakening the required route/wire outcomes.
